WORKED EXAMPLE 4 — SAME ANGLE, DIFFERENT SIZES
A 9–12–15 triangle and a 15–20–25 triangle have the same acute angle opposite their shorter leg. Compare sine and tangent.
Sine: 9/15=15/25=3/5. Tangent: 9/12=15/20=3/4. Both are unchanged.
WORKED EXAMPLE 5 — PYTHAGORAS AND SCALE
A right triangle has legs 8 and 15; a similar triangle has hypotenuse 51. Find the corresponding shorter leg.
Original hypotenuse is √(8²+15²)=17. Scale factor=51/17=3, so shorter leg=8×3=24.
DETERMINISTIC SIMILAR-TRIANGLE VISUAL
Compare the 3–4–5 right triangle with the 6–8–10 right triangle; both share an acute angle with opposite/adjacent=3/4.
Coordinates are generated using a scale factor of 2; both triangles have sine=3/5, cosine=4/5, tangent=3/4.
DESMOS STRATEGY
Check corresponding ratios numerically when sides have inconvenient lengths.
Enter 3/5 and 6/10, then 3/4 and 6/8. Each pair gives equal decimals; ratio cancellation is faster for simple numbers.
COMMON MISTAKES
Do not compare unmatched angles or use different side labels across similar triangles. Hypotenuse always faces the right angle.
Area scales by k², lengths scale by k, but sine/cosine/tangent do not scale.
EXAM STRATEGY
Match the reference angles, identify the three sides, then cancel the common scale factor before calculating.
If one side is missing, find the scale factor from a known corresponding pair; use Pythagoras only when needed.
QUICK CHECK
A 5–12–13 triangle is scaled by 4. For the angle opposite 5, what are sine, cosine, and tangent in both triangles?
sin=5/13, cos=12/13, tan=5/12 in both; the scaled triangle is 20–48–52.
LESSON RECAP
Similar right triangles have identical acute angles and identical trig ratios, even though their corresponding sides have different lengths.
sin=O/H, cos=A/H, tan=O/A; a common positive scale factor cancels.
